name: starlink_5285_skku_downlink_pass_v1
objective: Compare the BER of OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM under the same SKKU–STARLINK-5285 downlink conditions and the same received Eb/N0.

radio.carrier_frequency_basis: Representative Ku-band frequency for the four-scheme BER comparison; not a measured channel assignment for STARLINK-5285.
radio.bandwidth_basis: One-quarter of the observed 240 MHz Starlink Ku channel width for computational tractability, retaining the observed subcarrier spacing; this is a simulation choice, not the measured bandwidth of STARLINK-5285. The initial BER comparison uses all 256 bins without edge guard or DC null bins; guard/DC sensitivity studies and measured spectral occupancy remain for later.

sampling_model.sample_rate_basis: Fs = frequency_bin_count * subcarrier_spacing_hz = 256 * 234375 Hz = 60 MHz, without additional oversampling.
sampling_model.scope: Use the same sample rate for all four schemes in the initial controlled LOS plus AWGN, perfectly common-Doppler-compensated baseline. This is a digital baseband simulation choice, not a physical RF ADC specification or a permanent rate for every later experiment.
sampling_model.note: Equal sample rate alone does not ensure equal bandwidth, frame duration, data-bit count, energy, channel, receiver knowledge, or overhead. Pulse shaping and physical RF filtering are not selected by this sampling decision.

higher_rate_validation.purpose: Check sampling adequacy as more detailed multipath, Doppler, filtering, or waveform measurements are introduced.
higher_rate_validation.method: Repeat all four schemes on finer time grids and check BER convergence within Monte Carlo uncertainty. If waveform metrics such as PAPR or spectra are measured, also check convergence of those metrics before drawing conclusions.
higher_rate_validation.energy_and_noise_accounting: When comparing rates, account for the sample interval in physical energy or use an explicitly equivalent normalized coordinate convention. Recalculate waveform-sample scaling and noise variance; do not blindly reuse raw-sample noise settings.
higher_rate_validation.delay_accounting: Keep excess delays in seconds fixed and update their discrete representation when sample rate changes. The stored 2- and 5-sample delays are references at 60 MHz only.

constellation_normalization.scope: Use the same fixed constellation scaling for data symbols in OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM; do not rescale each random frame to force its empirical average to one.
constellation_normalization.units: Relative simulation energy units, not a physical transmit-power assignment of 1 watt.
constellation_normalization.note: All four schemes use the same Gray bit mapping, a data-symbol-only Eb reference, unitary useful-signal transforms, and the agreed 60 MHz baseline sample grid. Pilot energy, filtering, and any corresponding changes to the waveform-sample noise mapping remain to be designed.

waveform_transform_normalization.scope: Modulation and demodulation basis transforms on the useful frame, before prefix insertion and after prefix removal; this is not a constraint on the propagation channel or equalizer gain.
waveform_transform_normalization.energy_invariant: sum(|x_useful|^2) = sum(|s_grid|^2) on the same normalized discrete sample basis. Include explicitly allocated pilot energy in s_grid if pilots are later inserted.
waveform_transform_normalization.fourier_block_rule: Scale each length-L forward and inverse DFT block by 1/sqrt(L); apply this per transformed axis in two-dimensional Fourier mappings.
waveform_transform_normalization.daft_rule: Use a unitary Fourier block and unit-magnitude chirp factors for the DAFT/IDAFT pair; this does not choose AFDM chirp parameters.
waveform_transform_normalization.frame_scaling: Use fixed analytic transform factors; do not rescale each random frame to a forced empirical signal power or energy.
waveform_transform_normalization.prefix_and_pilot_energy: Preserve pilot energy through the useful-signal transforms when present. Count energy introduced by prefixes or other added samples separately; do not hide overhead by renormalizing the complete transmitted frame.
waveform_transform_normalization.note: The initial sample grid is fixed separately in sampling_model. OTFS uses the agreed rectangular transmit/receive windows. The first three-path stage uses the common five-sample slot CP, agreed native pilot masks and fixed known pilot values. Physical RF filtering and remaining channel estimation/equalization details are pending.

frame_design.prefixed_timing_scope: First pilot-based three-path comparison only. The without_prefix values remain the useful-grid and initial baseline references; no prefix is added to the initial single-path baseline by this decision.
frame_design.basis: Adopt 64 nominal time symbols on the agreed 256-bin, 234.375 kHz grid as the initial working frame. This is a computational starting choice, not an orbit-derived or validated optimal length. The DD-a-OFDM reference uses a different subcarrier spacing and frame duration. The first three-path stage has a five-sample CP per 256-sample block, agreed native pilot masks and fixed known pilot values; receiver design, runtime, and frame-length sensitivity remain pending.

frame_length_review.baseline_check: Compare BER estimates and execution time at alternative frame lengths while keeping the same uncoded Gray 16-QAM, energy/noise normalization, and ideal single-path AWGN conditions. Accumulate sufficient bits and errors; matched ideal implementations should agree within Monte Carlo uncertainty.
frame_length_review.later_channel_review: At fixed subcarrier spacing, changing the number of time symbols changes physical frame duration and Doppler-grid spacing. Assess channel/estimator suitability and report these resource changes; do not require BER to stay unchanged in a time-varying or multipath channel. Use matched frame resources across the four schemes at each chosen length.

selection_rule.c1_doppler_basis: Use the maximum absolute orbit-derived common LOS Doppler before receiver compensation over the selected visible pass as the design reference.

current_pass_doppler_reference.note: Numerical estimate for the current pinned-orbit draft pass, not a measured or universal Starlink maximum. Recompute if the pass, orbit, carrier, station, sample grid, or AFDM block length changes.

selection_rule.c1_delay_basis: Also account for the agreed three-path control profile's maximum excess delay: 5 samples at 60 MHz, approximately 83.3 ns.

c1_numeric_formula.integer_doppler_convention: nu = f_D / (F_s / N_AFDM) = alpha + a, with integer alpha and -0.5 < a <= 0.5. alpha_max is the maximum absolute integer component over the design envelope, not the Doppler at every snapshot.
c1_numeric_formula.alpha_max_basis: The current pass has maximum absolute normalized Doppler 1.11372416, so the integer component ranges from -1 to 1.

c1_validation.note: xi_nu = 1 is an agreed initial engineering choice, not a validated optimum or a guarantee that fractional-Doppler leakage is confined to one bin. The channel must retain the actual fractional Doppler. Pilot and guard allocations, and any receiver channel-matrix truncation, remain separate decisions.
c1_validation.followup: Assess the margin when multipath and receiver processing are introduced; explicitly review the fixed design if the adopted delay-Doppler envelope changes. The initial perfectly common-Doppler-compensated LOS AWGN baseline cannot establish this margin's Doppler robustness.

selection_rule.c1_application: Keep the selected c1 = 5/512 across baseline frames, Eb/N0 points, and low/high snapshot comparisons within the adopted design envelope; do not retune it per realization or snapshot. Revisit the design explicitly if that envelope changes.

c2_selection.basis: The AFDM paper motivates irrational c2 for the signal-difference matrix rank criterion under its path-separation and channel conditions. The specific sqrt(2)/N_AFDM**2 expression is our reproducible engineering choice, not a formula prescribed by the paper or a validated BER optimum.
c2_selection.scaling_rationale: The exact design expression is irrational; scaling by N_AFDM**2 keeps c2*m**2 on an order-one scale across a block. Numerical implementation uses a float64 approximation.
c2_selection.rank_criterion: For every nonzero allowed symbol-vector difference delta, Phi(delta) = [H_1*delta, ..., H_P*delta] should have column rank P. For N_AFDM=256 and the planned three paths this is a 256-by-3 matrix with target rank 3, distinct from the rank of the unitary DAFT matrix.
c2_selection.path_scope: Use the same selected c2 for the initial single-path baseline and the planned LOS plus two reflections with excess delays 0, 2, and 5 samples at 60 MHz.
c2_selection.application: Keep c2 fixed across frames, Eb/N0 points, and low/high snapshots in the adopted design envelope. Revisit the design explicitly if the block length or delay-Doppler envelope changes.

numerical_validation.block_model: Ideal cyclic delays with unit-gain per-path operators and zero residual common Doppler; excludes path gain coefficients, AWGN, pilots, and prefix implementation.
numerical_validation.note: A finite numerical screen cannot establish rank for every possible 256-symbol 16-QAM difference or guarantee BER/diversity performance. The first perfectly compensated single-path baseline cannot validate three-path diversity. The fixed-magnitude, LOS-dominant control channel also does not establish diversity order 3 merely from having three paths.

selection_rule.baseline_compensation: The initial single-path receiver still perfectly removes the actual common Doppler, leaving 0 Hz residual. Using a pre-compensation design reference does not change this channel assumption.
selection_rule.future_channel_scope: No nonzero differential path Doppler or uncompensated-Doppler experiment is introduced by this design-reference decision.

AFDM.comparison_basis: Align each 256-sample AFDM useful block with one 256-point OFDM IFFT symbol, and use 64 consecutive blocks in the common frame at 60 MHz. The N used for AFDM chirp-parameter selection is the per-block DAFT length 256, not the full-frame sample count 16384.
AFDM.prefix_pilot_and_receiver_details: The first three-path stage uses five prefix samples per 256-sample block. With the current even N=256 and integer 2*N*c1=5, AFDM's CPP equals the common ordinary CP. The native pilot mask and fixed values are implemented. DAFT-domain linear MMSE is the agreed equalizer family; the channel-estimation algorithm, matrix construction, processing extent and receiver implementation remain pending.
AFDM.note: A single 16384-point frame-wide DAFT is not selected for the initial baseline; its different spreading interval would be a separate waveform design. Matching useful block timing alone does not settle every fairness condition.

OTFS.array_convention: DD grid X_dd[l,k]: axis 0 is delay l, axis 1 is Doppler k. TF grid X_tf[m,n]: axis 0 is subcarrier m, axis 1 is time slot n. Both arrays have shape (256,64).
transmit_basis_steps: unitary IFFT along the 64-bin Doppler axis
unitary FFT along the 256-bin delay axis, completing the ISFFT
unitary 256-point IFFT along the frequency axis for each of 64 time slots
in the first three-path stage, copy the last five useful samples to the start of each slot
serialize each complete time slot in order
receive_basis_steps: remove the per-slot CP from aligned samples when present, then reshape into 64 consecutive 256-sample useful slots
unitary 256-point FFT along the within-slot sample axis
unitary IFFT along the frequency axis and FFT along the time axis, completing the SFFT
return DD observations for later channel equalization and symbol detection
OTFS.serialization: Useful-only slot n contains q=0,...,255 contiguously at index q+256*n, equivalent to order='F' on a (256,64) array. With CP, useful samples occur at q+L_CP+(256+L_CP)*n in the transmitted stream. No fftshift is applied inside the transforms.

pulse_shape.definition: Use the ordinary OFDM IFFT/FFT basis over each 256-sample useful slot. Unitary transform factors set the discrete energy normalization; no additional shaping gain or frame-power normalization is applied.
pulse_shape.physical_filter_scope: This useful-slot window choice does not select a DAC/RF filter or an occupied-bandwidth mask.

implementation.scope: Reusable ISFFT, SFFT, modulation and basis demodulation. Optional cp_length adds/removes a per-slot CP internally; the default cp_length=0 preserves useful-only transforms. Callers provide aligned samples. This is not the full BER transceiver.

validation.full_grid_cases: 8 random normalized 16-QAM grids and 4 DD impulses
validation.scope: Noiseless useful-signal transform checks only; no channel, prefix, pilot, synchronization, equalization, detection, or BER run.

pending_design: select and validate channel estimation for the agreed DD pilot mask and known pilot value
remaining receiver knowledge
channel-matrix construction, processing extent and implementation of the agreed DD linear-MMSE equalizer
symbol detection and complete four-waveform BER implementation
OTFS.reference_note: Use the documented ISFFT-plus-OFDM architecture with our agreed unitary normalization; do not copy the example's numerical scaling, channel, padding, or pilot parameters.

DD-a-OFDM.transmitter_basis: Conventional OFDM with the common unitary 256-point IFFT and 64 time symbols; data stay in the TF grid.

sections: IV-A and Algorithm 1: DD-domain ML channel estimation

reference_receiver_flow: OFDM FFT produces the received TF grid
known TF pilot observations form the sampled channel response
DD processing of the pilot observations estimates path delay, Doppler, and complex gain
reconstruct each OFDM symbol's TF channel matrix, including ICI terms
equalize TF data and perform QAM detection

receiver_design.channel_estimator: DD-domain ML using alternating projection with path-wise delay/Doppler searches and joint LS gain refinement, following Algorithm 1
receiver_design.equalizer: TF-domain ICI-aware full-matrix linear MMSE, following equations (43)-(44)
receiver_design.processing_rule: Estimate channel parameters from pilot observations under the shared receiver-information policy, reconstruct the TF channel matrix from those estimates, and apply linear MMSE to recover data symbols before QAM decisions. ML here is channel estimation, not exhaustive ML detection of the transmitted data vector.
receiver_design.scope: The initial algorithm combination, pilot spacing/mask, prefix, known pilot values and common 0..5-sample excess-delay support are agreed. Noise-variance knowledge, Doppler search bounds, fractional refinement, iteration settings, and corresponding receiver choices for other schemes remain pending; the full receiver has not been implemented.

selected_receiver_information.note: Use the shared receiver_information_policy. Future multipath common-Doppler compensation remains a separate decision; the initial single-path baseline's perfect common-Doppler knowledge is preserved.

pending_design: validate pilot-based estimation with the agreed TF mask and fixed known symbols
OFDM pulse/filter details beyond the shared cyclic-prefix rule
Doppler search support and fractional refinement within the common excess-delay bounds
initialization, iteration count and convergence criterion
noise-variance knowledge
comparable OFDM, AFDM and OTFS receiver processing
DD-a-OFDM.comparison_interpretation: OFDM and DD-a-OFDM use the same transmitted waveform when given the same TF symbols, pilots, and prefix/pulse configuration. BER differences then evaluate channel estimation and receiver processing as part of the transceiver comparison.
DD-a-OFDM.channel_scope: The shared P=3 receiver-information assumption applies to the first future three-path comparison. Keep the current single-path baseline, common-Doppler compensation policy, three-path generator profile, and zero additional path Dopplers unchanged; no additional Doppler experiment is introduced.

prefix_policy.basis: Use the maximum excess delay relative to LOS in the agreed 0/2/5-sample profile, not the absolute satellite-to-ground propagation delay.
prefix_policy.sample_time_rule: The full serial clock includes CP samples. Useful sample q in slot n occurs at ((256+5)*n+5+q)/F_s relative to the first transmitted CP sample; use this clock in channel Doppler phases and reconstruction.
prefix_policy.timing_assumption: Aligned block windows and the current integer-sample excess-delay model. Five is the minimum for that model; added timing uncertainty, fractional-delay/filter tails or a larger delay range require explicit review.

afdm_cpp_equivalence.condition: N is even and 2*N*c1 is an integer. Recheck this condition if the AFDM design changes; the generic helper does not implement an arbitrary chirp-periodic prefix.

prefix_policy.otfs_placement: CP on every 256-sample time slot; this is not a single reduced prefix on the entire OTFS frame.
prefix_policy.energy_accounting: Copy the tail samples without amplitude rescaling. Measure each frame's CP energy separately as the sum of squared copied-sample magnitudes; do not assume equal CP energy merely from equal CP lengths. Preserve data Es=1, the pilot energy budget, and the data-only Eb/N0 noise rule.
prefix_policy.baseline_scope: The initial single-path LOS AWGN stage and its common-Doppler compensation are unchanged. The new per-slot CP is selected for the followup three-path comparison; no multipath Doppler-compensation policy is selected here.

validation.useful_only_otfs_regression: python check_otfs_transform.py passed with its existing 1e-12 tolerance
validation.scope: Aligned integer-delay static three-path diagnostic without noise. The short-CP value is waveform mismatch, not BER. No receiver channel knowledge, multipath Doppler-compensation policy, estimator, equalizer or BER run is introduced.

receiver_equalization_policy.channel_source: Construct each channel operator from that receiver's pilot-based channel estimates under receiver_information_policy. Do not supply the true delays, additional path Dopplers or gains from the channel generator.
receiver_equalization_policy.interference_modeling: The agreed target is matrix-based linear MMSE accounting for interference represented by each estimated channel operator. How OFDM obtains its ICI terms, the other native matrix constructions and their processing extents remain to be designed; a common algorithm name alone does not establish equal receiver capability.

processing_window.joint_estimation_rule: Fit one time-varying channel model using the frame's available pilots, then evaluate that model at each OFDM block's sample times. The modeled channel varies throughout the window; shared BEM coefficients do not mean a static channel.
processing_window.frame_boundary_rule: Estimate each frame independently. Do not pool observations from adjacent independently redrawn channel-phase realizations as though they belonged to the same channel model.
processing_window.waveform_and_equalizer_scope: The transmitter remains 64 separate 256-point OFDM blocks. This decision selects the channel-estimation window only; it does not select a frame-wide data equalizer or its matrix dimensions.

decision_record.alternative_single_block: Shorter local model, but only even-numbered blocks 0,2,...,62 contain pilots in the selected TF lattice. Odd blocks have no direct pilots and need neighboring estimates, interpolation or an additional model; an isolated pilot-only per-block estimator does not cover the entire frame.
decision_record.selected_frame_window: Use all 32 pilot-bearing time positions within the already-agreed frame. This matches the channel-profile assumption that path delays, magnitudes and initial-phase parameters are fixed within the frame while differential Doppler induces deterministic phase evolution.
decision_record.boundary_basis: Independent trials redraw reflection initial phases, so the common 64-block frame is the initial natural modeling boundary. Keeping the window within a frame avoids assuming phase continuity across independent realizations.
decision_record.phase_cycle_calculation: 46875 Hz * 0.0002784 s = 13.05 cycles for a path at the maximum residual magnitude; this is not the phase rotation of the composite multipath channel.
decision_record.tradeoff: The longer window provides observations across the frame but requires a basis capable of representing its faster temporal variations. It is a selected initial design, not a measured optimum or proof of stable coefficient recovery.
decision_record.reference_scope: Literature precedent for multi-block BEM channel estimation and LS; our 64-block length follows this project's frame, pilot lattice and channel assumptions, not a prescribed value from the paper.

basis_design.rule: Use the previously reviewed fixed maximum residual envelope and CP-inclusive frame clock. Do not rebuild the basis from a trial's actual path Dopplers or current A/B sweep level. Shared use of this Doppler design bound by the other receiver algorithms remains a comparison-design item.

coefficient_estimation_prototype.tap_model: h_l[n] approximately equals sum_q b_q[n]*c_lq for each integer delay candidate l=0,...,5 and q=0,...,30 on the CP-inclusive receive clock.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.observation_equation: y_p = A_p*c + i_data + e_BEM + w_p. A_p is built from the known pilot component only, using serial shifts, sample-level DPSS, CP removal and each block's unitary FFT, then selecting the agreed TF pilot coordinates.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.coefficient_order: Delay-major: all 31 basis coefficients for delay 0, then delay 1, through delay 5. Pilot observation rows follow column-major TF grid order.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.solver: Thin SVD pseudoinverse with machine-epsilon-times-max-matrix-dimension numerical rank tolerance. No regularization or iterative solver is selected.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.receiver_inputs: Public frame/basis/delay design bounds, fixed known pilots and received pilot-coordinate observations only. The builder does not read channel_model; estimation receives no true data or active path parameters and needs no noise variance.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.unknown_data_treatment: Keep unknown-data ICI in the ordinary-LS residual. Do not cancel with true data or assume this residual is white, Gaussian or independent of the channel. Statistical weighting or decision feedback remains unselected.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.known_path_count_use: The P=3 prior remains available, but this dense prototype fits all six candidate taps without path pruning or sparsity enforcement.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.diagnostic_scope: 16 independent diagnostic frames per A/B condition and count, with identical data/phases/noise streams across counts. Actual data and AWGN at the existing 0:5:30-dB Eb/N0 grid are included. This is channel-estimation validation, not a BER run or a change to the agreed bit quota.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.findings: Independent serial-channel and exact-BEM controls pass. Data ICI is negligible for static A and produces a nonzero ordinary-LS estimation floor for B. The pilot-free last block 63 is substantially less accurate. Among 29/30/31, 31 is best at maximum B-4 in this diagnostic, but 29 is better at some intermediate levels. Keep the agreed initial 31; do not adapt to a test level or declare a BER optimum.
coefficient_estimation_prototype.full_receiver_scope: The complete OFDM estimator remains provisional. No TF data equalizer, detector or four-way BER comparison has been implemented.

basis_review.selection_summary: The user agreed to DPSS/Slepian with 31 functions as the initial basis after comparing 29, 30 and 31. Prioritize lower representation error at the maximum residual Doppler; keep 29 and 30 as validation alternatives and retain DFT-grid complex exponentials as a comparison. This initial choice is not a demonstrated optimum or a validated estimator.
basis_review.design_envelope: Use the existing whole-frame CP-inclusive clock and fixed +/-46875-Hz maximum residual envelope, without adapting the basis to an actual path Doppler or Doppler test level.

initial_basis_decision.user_agreement: The user accepted 31 as the initial value after reviewing the added 30-function result and the representation/noise-sensitivity tradeoff.
initial_basis_decision.reason: Among these candidates, 31 gives the smallest worst-case best-fit trajectory error over the 401 diagnostic Dopplers. Prioritizing representation fidelity at the maximum residual Doppler is a design judgment for the first implementation, not a measured BER optimum.
initial_basis_decision.tradeoff: The worst relative L2 errors for 29/30/31 are approximately 9.91/3.92/1.46 percent, while ideal white-observation-noise channel-MSE gains relative to 29 are 1/1.85/3.22. More functions reduce representation error but increase this LS noise-sensitivity metric.
initial_basis_decision.even_count_note: 30 is a valid DPSS count and was explicitly evaluated. The original odd diagnostic counts aligned with the symmetric integer-frequency complex-exponential comparison and are not a DPSS parity requirement.
initial_basis_decision.validation_pending: An initial pilot-based channel-NMSE diagnostic now includes unknown-data ICI and AWGN for 29/30/31. Resolve the interference model and frame-end weakness, then validate full equalization and BER. The common 0..5-sample delay support is recorded in receiver_information_policy.delay_support; true active delays remain unavailable.

basis_review.pilot_matrix_scope: Exact native response of the known OFDM pilot component over all integer delays 0 through CP length 5, not the true three path locations. The same interval is now explicit common support in receiver_information_policy.delay_support.
basis_review.limitations: Best-fit trajectory representation and pilot-component rank/conditioning are diagnostics. The separate ordinary-LS prototype adds actual pilot-based channel-NMSE checks with data ICI and AWGN; interference treatment, frame-end accuracy and full BER remain unresolved. Full rank alone is insufficient.

pending_design: resolve the ordinary-LS unknown-data ICI residual before selecting the final estimator
remaining shared receiver priors including Doppler-bound availability to all receiver algorithms
frame-end block 63 accuracy under data ICI and AWGN
full channel-matrix reconstruction, equalizer details, detector and BER implementation
candidate_design.selection_note: The one-frame, 64-block estimation window, initial DPSS/Slepian 31-function basis and common 0..5-sample integer-delay bounds are agreed. An ordinary-LS prototype is implemented and diagnosed; the full estimator remains provisional because data ICI and frame-end estimation errors still need review.

receiver_equalization_policy.existing_DD_a_design: Preserve the selected DD-ML alternating-projection estimator and ICI-aware 256-by-256 TF linear-MMSE matrix for each of 64 symbols. The new common-family choice does not replace that design.
pending_design: OFDM BEM-LS data-interference and frame-end weaknesses; AFDM/OTFS channel-estimation algorithms
estimated-channel matrix reconstruction and equalizer processing extent for OFDM/AFDM/OTFS
pilot contribution handling and data-domain covariance accounting
remaining receiver priors, including common Doppler design-bound availability and noise-variance knowledge
equalizer numerical solver and any stopping settings
full receiver validation and BER implementation
receiver_equalization_policy.baseline_scope: The initial single-path LOS plus AWGN validation and its perfect common-frequency correction remain unchanged. This policy does not grant perfect multipath channel knowledge.
receiver_equalization_policy.reference_basis: Section V-D uses ICI-aware MMSE equalizers for the OFDM/DD-a-OFDM comparison. Extending the linear-MMSE family to all four native receivers is our agreed experimental choice; it does not require copying a source paper's estimator or detector for every waveform.
receiver_equalization_policy.other_equalizer_families: Not selected for the initial comparison. This status means an experimental choice is pending or excluded, not that other receiver methodologies do not exist in the literature.

receiver_information_policy.availability_rule: Make P=3 available equally to all four receivers. A receiver may use this prior when its algorithm supports it; this does not require every receiver to use a path-parametric estimator.

delay_support.reference: Excess delay relative to the aligned LOS receive window, at 60 MHz; not the absolute satellite-to-ground propagation time.
delay_support.availability_rule: Provide the same 0..5-sample support bound to all four receivers. Integer-delay candidates are 0,1,2,3,4,5; the actual active locations 0,2,5 are not supplied.
delay_support.basis: Use the already selected maximum excess delay and CP length. Fractional-delay modeling and any wider timing uncertainty require a separate review.

receiver_information_policy.parameter_estimation_rule: Obtain the channel response or path parameters from the agreed pilot observations. Do not copy the actual 0/2/5-sample delays, per-path Dopplers, or complex gains from the channel generator into the receivers.
receiver_information_policy.purpose: First compare channel-parameter estimation and BER without adding path-count detection errors. State this known-count assumption in reported results; equal path-count information alone does not settle other fairness conditions.
receiver_information_policy.baseline_scope: This policy does not change the initial single-path LOS AWGN baseline or its perfect common-Doppler knowledge and compensation. Future multipath compensation details remain to be discussed.
receiver_information_policy.remaining_receiver_design: All receivers share P=3 and 0..5-sample excess-delay bounds; true active path parameters remain unavailable. Linear MMSE remains the common equalizer family. OFDM's 64-block DPSS-31 ordinary-LS prototype now has channel-NMSE diagnostics with data ICI and AWGN, but its final interference treatment and frame-end accuracy remain unresolved. DD-a-OFDM's DD-ML/TF matrix-MMSE design is preserved. AFDM/OTFS estimators, detailed matrices/equalizers, common Doppler-bound availability, noise-variance knowledge, fractional search refinement, solver settings and complete BER implementation remain pending.

path_count_estimation_followup.purpose: Replace the known count with a receiver-estimated count and compare against the known-count reference. Assess missed or spurious paths and their impact on parameter estimation and BER.
path_count_estimation_followup.comparison_rule: Review the receiver-information and resource conditions for all four schemes before this extension; no scheme receives the true count as hidden assistance in an estimated-count comparison.

pilot_comparison_policy.fairness_interpretation: Compare four pilot-based transceiver designs under matched non-data resource and total useful-signal pilot-energy budgets. Native pilot counts, placements and channel estimators can differ. The equalizer family is linear MMSE for all four, while channel-matrix construction and processing extents still need specification. BER differences include those design effects; do not attribute all differences to intrinsic modulation-waveform behavior alone.
pilot_comparison_policy.pilot_plus_pilot_guard_resource_fraction: Use the same fraction of the frame's resources for pilots and pilot-specific guard or reserved cells across all four schemes.
pilot_comparison_policy.total_pilot_energy_rule: Match the total energy allocated to pilot signals across all four schemes; do not treat a higher-power pilot as free.
pilot_comparison_policy.total_pilot_energy_units: Normalized transmit energy per useful frame before the channel, with the existing average data-symbol energy E_s=1; excludes CP/CPP energy and is not power in watts.

initial_budget.budget_unit: One common 256-by-64 useful grid, with 16384 native complex-symbol degrees of freedom. Count the union of pilot and pilot-specific guard/reserved cells; count CP/CPP samples and energy separately.

energy_budget.allocation_rule: Uniform energy per active pilot within each scheme: |x_p|^2 = E_p/N_p. OFDM/DD-a-OFDM use energy 1, AFDM uses 64 and OTFS uses 4096 per active cell, all in E_s units. Match total pilot energy across schemes; do not rescale data or individual frames.
energy_budget.note: Normalized simulation energy, not watts. Known phases are fixed in known_pilot_sequence. OFDM/DD-a-OFDM have 4096 pilots of magnitude 1, AFDM has 64 of magnitude 8, and OTFS has one 64+0j pilot. Data remain uncoded Gray 16-QAM with E_s=1. Equality applies to useful transmit energy before the channel and CP; copied-prefix energy is recorded separately and is not automatically equal.

initial_budget.ofdm_and_dd_a_rule: Use identical TF pilot positions, known pilot values, and pilot energy distribution for the OFDM/DD-a-OFDM pair.
initial_budget.native_layout_rule: AFDM uses DAFT-domain pilot/guard placement and OTFS uses DD-domain placement. Design each actual mask within the common non-data budget; do not force identical coordinates across different bases.
initial_budget.reporting_rule: Record each scheme's nonzero pilot count, pilot-specific guard/reserved count, data count, and total pilot energy separately, in addition to the common combined overhead fraction.

conditional_afdm_budget_screen.layout_assumption: One embedded pilot in each 256-point AFDM block is now selected; the agreed mask expands the cited 59-cell pilot-plus-guard count to 64 cells by adding five zero guards per block.
conditional_afdm_budget_screen.note: A conditional resource count, not a universal minimum or a leakage-free guarantee. It uses the current AFDM design bounds and margin; full fractional-Doppler leakage and receiver performance still require validation. Different pilot layouts or Doppler support can change the budget.

initial_budget.selection_basis: The agreed initial 25-percent budget is a convenient rounding above the conditional 59/256 AFDM count. It is not an optimized ratio or a demonstrated minimum for all four schemes; uniform per-block allocation is not imposed by this frame-level budget.
remaining_checks: check pilot-data leakage, identifiability and estimation accuracy for all four native layouts using the selected fixed pilot values
measure CP energy under the agreed prefix_policy and account for full-frame energy costs
preserve the agreed information-bit quota when framing data and padding

known_pilot_sequence.hash_encoding: SHA256 of the 4096 integer phase indices converted to uint8 bytes, in sequence order.
known_pilot_sequence.OFDM_and_DD_a_OFDM: Use identical full master phase sequences, each multiplied by magnitude 1.
known_pilot_sequence.AFDM: Use the first 64 entries of the same master phase sequence, each multiplied by magnitude 8, in block order.
known_pilot_sequence.OTFS: Single known pilot 64+0j, with phase zero.
known_pilot_sequence.reuse_rule: Generate deterministically from a dedicated local RNG. Reuse the same values across frames, independent BER trials, Eb/N0 points, A/B Doppler levels and orbit snapshots; do not draw from data-bit or random channel-phase streams.
known_pilot_sequence.receiver_knowledge: All transmitted pilot values are known a priori at their corresponding receivers. This does not reveal unknown channel delays, differential Dopplers or complex path gains.
known_pilot_sequence.selection_basis: Reproducible initial constant-modulus pilot choice; not a validated optimum or a paper-mandated sequence. Data modulation remains 16-QAM.

shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.index_origin_convention: Use zero-based array coordinates and place the first pilot at (frequency=0, time=0); this fixes a reproducible grid origin for the agreed spacing.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.pilot_index_rule: Pilot at (m,n) iff m % 2 == 0 and n % 2 == 0, for 0 <= m < 256 and 0 <= n < 64. All remaining TF cells carry data.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.paired_rule: Use exactly the same mask, known pilot values and energy allocation for OFDM and DD-a-OFDM. Keep this layout fixed across A and all B levels; the separately agreed AFDM/OTFS native-domain masks use the same overhead and total pilot energy budgets.
shared_ofdm_dd_a_tf_layout.energy_note: Every active pilot has energy 1, with fixed QPSK phases and identical values for OFDM/DD-a-OFDM. Total useful-signal pilot energy is 4096; CP energy remains separate.

basic_sampling_screen.interpretation: The uniform TF sample model's basic delay period is 1/(d_f*Delta_f), and symmetric Doppler alias bound is 1/(2*d_t*T_block), with CP included in T_block. The agreed delay profile and residual Doppler envelope fit these basic ranges; this is not a proof of fractional-Doppler leakage suppression, path identifiability or BER performance.

afdm_daft_layout.placement_note: Zero-based cyclic DAFT coordinates: one pilot at zero, with 31 zero guards before it and 32 after it. Repeat in all 64 blocks and all A/B conditions.
afdm_daft_layout.validation_note: The 64-cell non-data mask contains the cited 59-cell mask under the agreed c1/margin bounds. Fractional-Doppler tails remain present; this is not a leakage-free or BER guarantee.

otfs_dd_layout.placement_note: Place one pilot at the DD-grid center. Reserve 64 delay rows across all 64 Doppler columns; all cells in this region except the pilot are zero. Keep the same mask for A and every B level.
otfs_dd_layout.resource_note: The 704-cell full-Doppler guard region includes the pilot. The other 3392 cells are extra zero reservations to match the agreed 25-percent comparison budget, not a claimed minimum guard requirement.
otfs_dd_layout.validation_note: The full-Doppler guard construction is a starting layout for the agreed integer excess delays and per-slot CP. Validate with the exact native channel; no complete estimator, equalizer or BER result is implied.

validation.scope: Use the agreed fixed pilots and uniform energy split. Check repeatability, shared basic phase values, isolated-pilot useful-signal energy before CP and native-grid roundtrips. The OTFS data-only guard diagnostic uses aligned integer delays 0/2/5 and every agreed residual Doppler level; it is not a channel estimator or BER test. AFDM fractional-Doppler estimation leakage remains pending.

pilot_comparison_policy.note: Native masks, known pilot values and uniform per-scheme pilot energy allocation are implemented. build_grid uses the selected fixed pilots by default and still accepts explicitly supplied values for controlled diagnostics, without rescaling them. Keep 25-percent non-data resources and 4096-E_s useful-signal pilot energy. CP energy remains separate. No completed channel estimator or four-way BER simulation is supplied here.

baseline.purpose: First validate the four transceivers and their energy/noise normalization in a single-path LOS plus complex AWGN channel with perfectly known and fully corrected common Doppler; this stage does not test Doppler robustness.

multipath_followup.profile_basis: Agreed synthetic, LOS-dominant three-path comparison condition; not a measurement of the SKKU–STARLINK-5285 channel or a standardized NTN profile.
multipath_followup.doppler_model: Apply the orbit-derived LOS Doppler at each snapshot to all three paths, with zero additional per-path Doppler as a first approximation for a fixed ground station and stationary local reflectors. This does not model differential Doppler spread.

doppler_effect_followup.purpose: After single-path baseline validation, compare the agreed three-path delay profile with zero residual Doppler (A) against the same profile with progressively larger differential path Doppler (B).
doppler_effect_followup.per_path_doppler_model: Controlled synthetic differential-Doppler sweep, not measured or geometry-derived SKKU reflection Doppler. At each agreed maximum residual magnitude d, use [0, +d, -d] in the fixed path order [los, reflection_1, reflection_2]. The sign assignment is the same across levels and all four schemes.

sweep_magnitude_design.definition: d = max_p(abs(delta_f_p)), where delta_f_p is each path's residual Doppler after perfect common LOS correction; delta_f_LOS = 0. This is a maximum magnitude relative to LOS, not the full signed Doppler spread max(delta_f_p)-min(delta_f_p).
sweep_magnitude_design.interpretation: Five exploratory conditions total: zero Doppler is A, and the four positive maximum magnitudes define B-1 through B-4. Levels are an agreed synthetic sensitivity-study choice, not measured Starlink differential Doppler or a standard-mandated grid.
sweep_magnitude_design.sampling_note: Preserve the physical Doppler frequencies without rounding to integer DD bins. Re-evaluate the normalization explicitly if the common subcarrier spacing changes.

common_doppler_compensation_policy.common_doppler_source: Orbit-derived LOS shift at the selected snapshot, shared by all paths before their additional offsets.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.receiver_knowledge: Provide the exact common LOS frequency for correction before waveform-specific demodulation. Do not provide the additional reflection-path Dopplers, delays, or complex gains; the agreed P=3 prior remains available to all four receivers.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.correction: Apply exp(-j*2*pi*f_LOS*n/F_s) after channel summation and receiver AWGN, with a continuous sample time including the per-block prefixes.
common_doppler_compensation_policy.per_path_residual_after_correction: additional_doppler_hz_to_los; it is zero on LOS in both A and B.

signed_reflection_doppler_pattern.path_binding: reflection_1 retains excess delay 2 samples and relative power -10 dB; reflection_2 retains excess delay 5 samples and relative power -15 dB. Do not swap the Doppler signs between paths or trials.

paired_conditions.comparison_control: At each Eb/N0, reuse a trial's path magnitudes and initial phases across A, B sweep levels, and all four schemes. Only the selected differential Doppler changes. Keep a fixed finalized pilot design and receiver settings across the sweep unless an explicitly agreed common adaptation rule is introduced.
paired_conditions.snapshot_interpretation: If the residual profile is the same, perfect common correction makes peak and exit equivalent residual-Doppler conditions. The synthetic B levels, rather than the raw orbit shifts, define the Doppler stress.

doppler_effect_followup.within_frame_evolution: Initial phases and path magnitudes stay fixed per trial; B adds deterministic exp(j*2*pi*delta_f_p*t) path phase rotation with continuous time including prefixes. No additional random phase or amplitude evolution is selected.
pending_design: Pilot-mask feasibility and receiver estimation search support for the agreed residual envelope
doppler_effect_followup.note: The existing explicit zero-additional-Doppler profile supplies A. B overrides only its path Dopplers using the agreed signed vectors above; delays, powers, normalization and paired initial phases remain unchanged. These are selected settings, not an implemented channel generator or BER results. Imperfect common correction is a separate unselected extension.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.path_magnitudes: Fixed at the agreed relative powers throughout each frame; no within-frame amplitude fading in the first comparison.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.relative_phases: Draw a new random initial reflection-path phase combination for each independent BER trial and keep these initial-phase parameters fixed within that trial; deterministic common and condition-B differential Doppler rotations are applied separately.

phase_distribution.reflection_phases_rad: Independent continuous uniform draws on [0, 2*pi) for each BER trial.

path_phase_and_gain_realization.paired_comparison: Reuse the same initial relative-phase realization for OFDM, AFDM, OTFS, and DD-a-OFDM, the low/high snapshots, and the paired A/B sweep levels within a trial.
path_phase_and_gain_realization.within_frame_time_variation: The explicit zero-additional-Doppler profile retains only common orbit-derived phase rotation. Condition B additionally uses deterministic differential-Doppler phase rotation as defined in doppler_effect_followup; no random amplitude or phase evolution is added.

power_normalization.common_complex_gain_scale: 1/sqrt(sum_p(P_p)); apply once to all path gains so sum_p(|h_p|^2) = 1 while preserving the agreed relative powers.
power_normalization.scope: Channel-profile level, not a per-frame or per-frequency-bin received-power adjustment.
power_normalization.receiver_noise: The data-symbol-reference AWGN variance, conditional unitary-transform sample rule, and initial 60 MHz sample grid are defined separately. Any later resampling or filter effects require revised sample-domain accounting; implementation is still pending.

noise_model.injection_point: Once at the receiver, after the LOS and any reflected signal paths are combined.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.reference_noise_generation: n_s = sqrt(sigma_s^2/2)*(u + j*v), with independent u,v drawn from N(0,1).

waveform_sample_mapping.condition: Use the agreed square unitary transmit/receive basis transforms on the same discrete sample grid, without additional resampling or filtering gain.
waveform_sample_mapping.note: Unitary receiver basis transforms preserve white complex AWGN covariance. The initial sample grid is 60 MHz without additional oversampling or resampling. Re-derive the sample-domain scaling if later sampling or filtering introduces additional factors; this rule does not select physical filter settings.

received_eb_n0_to_noise_variance_rule.note: Use the agreed data-symbol energy and analytic transform factors on the initial 60 MHz grid. Do not infer noise variance from each random frame's instantaneous measured power. Additional physical filtering remains a separate design decision.

noise_model.basis: A controlled first BER comparison; interference, phase noise, and other real-link impairments are not included in this noise model.

receiver_doppler_compensation.receiver_knowledge: The receiver is given exactly the same snapshot common-Doppler value used by the channel generator, without estimation error.
receiver_doppler_compensation.correction: After channel and receiver AWGN, multiply received samples by exp(-j*2*pi*f_D*n/F_s) to remove the common snapshot frequency shift before waveform-specific demodulation.
receiver_doppler_compensation.note: This entry remains scoped to the single-path baseline. The separately agreed A/B three-path policy is in channel_model.multipath_followup.doppler_effect_followup; imperfect common correction remains unselected.

doppler_comparison.doppler_value_source: Computed, not chosen: -carrier_frequency_hz * slant_range_rate / speed_of_light, with slant-range rate estimated by a 1-second centered difference; Doppler values rounded to 0.1 Hz.
doppler_comparison.baseline_snapshot_interpretation: Keep the original low/high snapshot shifts as orbit-derived inputs. Both have zero residual common Doppler under perfect correction; their BER statistics should coincide at equal received Eb/N0 with other conditions matched. They are not distinct Doppler-stress conditions in the initial baseline.
doppler_comparison.basis: Retain peak elevation and the visible-pass exit at 10 degrees as the original low/high snapshot references. First validate the perfectly common-Doppler-compensated single-path baseline, then compare paired three-path A/B conditions under the separate agreed common-correction policy. Maximum residual Doppler magnitudes and the signed [0,+d,-d] path pattern are agreed; pilot feasibility and receiver search settings remain pending. Recompute times and shifts if the draft pass changes.

result_interpretation.comparison_scope: Resource- and energy-budget-matched comparison of four pilot-based transceiver designs, including their native pilot/channel-estimation/equalization effects; this is not a perfect-CSI isolation of intrinsic waveform differences.
result_interpretation.swept_input: Common received data-symbol-referenced E_b/N_0 in dB; use the existing exploratory sweep and noise-normalization rules.
result_interpretation.measured_output: BER, measured as erroneous recovered information bits divided by measured transmitted information bits.
result_interpretation.fixed_eb_n0_comparison: At the same received E_b/N_0 and matched comparison conditions, lower BER indicates better reliability.
result_interpretation.target_ber_comparison: The same measured curves may also compare the E_b/N_0 required to reach a target BER, when the simulated range and statistical uncertainty support that comparison. A target BER is not selected here.
result_interpretation.snr_note: E_b/N_0 is a bit-energy to noise-spectral-density ratio related to waveform SNR, not an interchangeable label for sample-power SNR. BER is the primary measured performance metric; E_b/N_0 is the controlled horizontal axis.

eb_energy_reference.definition: Average normalized data-symbol energy per information bit: Eb = Es/bits_per_symbol for the initial uncoded comparison.
eb_energy_reference.note: Exclusion from Eb accounting does not decide whether pilots or guards are present in the transmitted waveform. Keep the agreed pilot resource/energy fairness policy; evaluate a total-frame-energy-per-information-bit reference separately when overhead is designed.

extension_tracking.interpretation: Index of discussed extensions and reviews, not a new execution order or selection of pending numerical parameters. The main extension_order remains the agreed staging rule; none of these BER extensions has been run.

evaluation.initial_stage_interpretation: Check basic transmitter/receiver behavior and energy/noise normalization against the common uncoded Gray-mapped 16-QAM AWGN reference under ideal processing. Similar BER is expected for matched ideal implementations; no Doppler-robustness ranking is inferred at this stage.

monte_carlo_measurement.counted_bits: Count transmitted information/data bits and their recovered counterparts; exclude known pilot, prefix, guard, and padding content from the BER denominator.
monte_carlo_measurement.framing_note: The 160-frame equivalence assumes all 256*64 grid cells carry uncoded 16-QAM data. Recompute framing when pilots or reserved cells are introduced while preserving the common information-bit quota; this decision does not select their allocation.

pilot_stage_framing_budget.note: Arithmetic for the agreed masks' 12288 data cells with 4 bits per symbol and the unchanged 10485760-bit quota. Final-frame padding/measurement handling remains to be designed; do not round the bit quota or count pilots/guards/padding as measured information bits.

monte_carlo_measurement.budget_basis: An initial approximately ten-million-bit budget gives about 100 expected errors if the true BER is 1e-5. This is a rough precision planning basis, not an error-count stopping target, a guaranteed error count, or a guarantee of precision at lower BER.

reporting.zero_error_interpretation: Record zero observed errors and the measured bit count without asserting that the true BER is exactly zero; report uncertainty using the selected interval method.

eb_n0_refinement.selection_basis: Select the region where BER changes or the four waveforms differ after the exploratory sweep; extend the bounds if needed.

evaluation.eb_n0_sweep_basis: A computationally economical initial scan, not a measured STARLINK-5285 receive SNR range.
evaluation.channel_coding_followup: deferred; apply the same code to all four waveforms if studied later
